text: The Human Intellect, even in an Unphilosophical State, is in Possession of Certain Cognitions “à priori”.
zh: 人类智力，即使处于非哲学状态，也拥有某些“先验”认知。
chunks: The Human Intellect,
even in an Unphilosophical State,
is in Possession
of Certain Cognitions “à priori”.

text: Transcendental Exposition of the Conception of Time.
zh: 时间概念的先验阐释。
chunks: Transcendental Exposition
of the Conception of Time.

text: Of the Supreme Principle of all Synthetical Judgements.
zh: 所有综合判断的最高原则。
chunks: Of the Supreme Principle
of all Synthetical Judgements.

text: Of the Interest of Reason in these Self-contradictions.
zh: 论理性对这些自相矛盾的兴趣。
chunks: Of the Interest
of Reason in these Self-contradictions.

text: Solution of the Cosmological Idea of the Totality of the Deduction of Cosmical Events from their Causes.
zh: 从原因推论宇宙事件整体性的宇宙学观念的解决方案。
chunks: Solution of the Cosmological Idea
of the Totality of the Deduction of Cosmical Events from their Causes.

text: Critique of all Theology based upon Speculative Principles of Reason.
zh: 基于理性思辨原则对所有神学的批判。
chunks: Critique of all Theology based
upon Speculative Principles of Reason.

text: Of Opinion, Knowledge, and Belief.
zh: 意见、知识和信仰。
chunks: Of Opinion, Knowledge,
and Belief.

text: The arena of these endless contests is called _Metaphysic_.
zh: 这些无休无止的竞赛的竞技场被称为_形而上学_。
chunks: The arena
of these endless contests is called _Metaphysic_.

text: [1] We very often hear complaints of the shallowness of the present age, and of the decay of profound science.
zh: [1] 我们经常听到人们抱怨当今时代的浅薄和深奥科学的衰落。
chunks: [1] We very often hear complaints
of the shallowness
of the present age,
and of the decay
of profound science.

text: The above remarks relate to the _matter_ of our critical inquiry.
zh: 上述言论与我们批判性调查的_问题_有关。
chunks: The above remarks relate
to the _matter_ of our critical inquiry.

text: But I beg to remind him that, if my subjective deduction does not produce in his mind the conviction of its certitude at which I aimed, the objective deduction, with which alone the present work is properly concerned, is in every respect satisfactory.
chunks: But I beg to remind him that,
if my subjective deduction does not produce in his mind the conviction
of its certitude at which I aimed, the objective deduction,
with which alone the present work is properly concerned,
is in every respect satisfactory.

text: The reader must naturally have a strong inducement to co-operate with the present author, if he has formed the intention of erecting a complete and solid edifice of metaphysical science, according to the plan now laid before him.
zh: 如果读者已经形成了按照现在摆在他面前的计划建造一座完整而坚固的形而上学大厦的意图，那么他自然会产生与作者合作的强烈动机。
chunks: The reader must naturally have a strong inducement
to co-operate with the present author,
if he has formed the intention of erecting a complete
and solid edifice of metaphysical science,
according to the plan now laid before him.

text: These cannot be presented _à priori_, but must be gradually discovered; and, while the _synthesis_ of conceptions has been fully exhausted in the Critique, it is necessary that, in the proposed work, the same should be the case with their _analysis_.
chunks: These cannot be presented _à priori_,
but must be gradually discovered; and, while the _synthesis_
of conceptions has been fully exhausted
in the Critique, it is necessary that, in the proposed work,
the same should be the case with their _analysis_.

text: It is, obviously, a much more difficult task for reason to strike into the sure path of science, where it has to deal not simply with itself, but with objects external to itself.
zh: 显然，理性要走上科学的正确道路是一项更加困难的任务，因为它不仅要处理自身，还要处理自身之外的对象。
chunks: It is, obviously, a much more difficult task
for reason to strike into the sure path
of science, where it has
to deal not simply with itself,
but with objects external to itself.

text: Still it is not to be supposed that it was as easy for this science to strike into, or rather to construct for itself, that royal road, as it was for logic, in which reason has only to deal with itself.
zh: 尽管如此，我们仍然不能认为这门科学很容易闯入，或者更确切地说，为自己构建一条康庄大道，就像逻辑一样，在逻辑中，理性只需要处理自身。
chunks: Still it is not to be supposed
that it was as easy for this science to strike into,
or rather to construct for itself, that royal road,
as it was for logic,
in which reason has only to deal with itself.

text: But it is this that reason seeks for and requires.
zh: 但这正是理性所寻求和要求的。
chunks: But it is this
that reason seeks for and requires.

text: We find that reason perpetually comes to a stand, when it attempts to gain _à priori_ the perception even of those laws which the most common experience confirms.
zh: 我们发现，当理性试图获得先验的感知，甚至是那些最常见的经验所证实的法则时，它就会永远陷入困境。
chunks: We find that reason perpetually comes
to a stand, when it attempts
to gain _à priori_ the perception even
of those laws
which the most common experience confirms.

text: This appears, at all events, to accord better with the _possibility_ of our gaining the end we have in view, that is to say, of arriving at the cognition of objects _à priori_, of determining something with respect to these objects, before they are given to us.
chunks: This appears, at all events, to accord better with the _possibility_
of our gaining the end we have in view, that is
to say, of arriving at the cognition of objects _à priori_,
of determining something with respect to these objects,
before they are given to us.

text: Now there are objects which reason _thinks_, and that necessarily, but which cannot be given in experience, or, at least, cannot be given _so_ as reason thinks them.
zh: 现在有些对象是理性所思考的，而且是必然的，但它们不能在经验中给出，或者至少不能像理性所认为的那样给出。
chunks: Now there are objects
which reason _thinks_, and that necessarily,
but which cannot be given
in experience, or, at least,
cannot be given _so_ as reason thinks them.

text: The estimate of our rational cognition _à priori_ at which we arrive is that it has only to do with phenomena, and that things in themselves, while possessing a real existence, lie beyond its sphere.
zh: 我们对理性认知的先验估计是，它只与现象有关，而事物本身虽然拥有真实的存在，但却超出了其范围。
chunks: The estimate of our rational cognition _à priori_
at which we arrive is
that it has only to do with phenomena,
and that things in themselves,
while possessing a real existence, lie beyond its sphere.

text: But, at the same time, it marks out and defines both the external boundaries and the internal structure of this science.
zh: 但同时，它也划定并定义了这门科学的外部边界和内部结构。
chunks: But, at the same time,
it marks
out and defines both the external boundaries
and the internal structure
of this science.

text: Now let us suppose, for a moment, that we had not undertaken this criticism and, accordingly, had not drawn the necessary distinction between things as objects of experience and things as they are in themselves.
zh: 现在让我们暂时假设，我们没有进行这种批评，因此，没有在作为经验对象的事物和事物本身之间做出必要的区分。
chunks: Now let us suppose, for a moment,
that we had not undertaken this criticism
and, accordingly, had not drawn the necessary distinction
between things as objects of experience and things
as they are in themselves.

text: But something more is required before I can attribute to such a conception objective validity, that is real possibility—the other possibility being merely logical.
zh: 但在我能够赋予这样一个概念客观有效性之前，还需要更多的东西，那就是真正的可能性——另一种可能性仅仅是逻辑上的。
chunks: But something more is required
before I can attribute
to such a conception objective validity,
that is real possibility—
the other possibility being merely logical.

text: It will render an important service to the inquiring mind of youth, by leading the student to apply his powers to the cultivation of genuine science, instead of wasting them, as at present, on speculations which can never lead to any result, or on the idle attempt to invent new ideas and opinions.
chunks: It will render an important service to the inquiring mind of youth,
by leading the student to apply his powers to the cultivation of genuine science,
instead of wasting them, as at present, on speculations
which can never lead to any result,
or on the idle attempt to invent new ideas and opinions.

text: Quod mecum nescit, solus vult scire videri.
zh: Quod mecum nescit, solus vult scire videri。
chunks: Quod mecum nescit,
solus vult scire videri.

text: He would have been peculiarly well fitted to give a truly scientific character to metaphysical studies, had it occurred to him to prepare the field by a criticism of the _organum_, that is, of pure reason itself.
zh: 如果他想到通过对有机体（即纯粹理性本身）的批评来准备形而上学研究，那么他将特别适合赋予形而上学研究真正的科学特征。
chunks: He would have been peculiarly well fitted
to give a truly scientific character
to metaphysical studies, had it occurred to him
to prepare the field by a criticism
of the _organum_, that is, of pure reason itself.

text: [8] The only addition, properly so called—and that only in the method of proof—which I have made in the present edition, consists of a new refutation of psychological _Idealism_, and a strict demonstration—the only one possible, as I believe—of the objective reality of external intuition.
chunks: [8] The only addition, properly so called— and that only
in the method of proof— which I have made in the present edition,
consists of a new refutation of psychological _Idealism_, and a strict demonstration—
the only one possible, as I believe—
of the objective reality of external intuition.

text: To the question _How?_ we are no more able to reply, than we are, in general, to think the stationary in time, the coexistence of which with the variable, produces the conception of change.
zh: 对于“如何？”这个问题，我们无法回答，正如我们一般无法思考时间的静止状态，它与变量的共存会产生变化的概念。
chunks: To the question _How?_ we are no more able
to reply, than we are,
in general, to think the stationary
in time, the coexistence of which with the variable,
produces the conception of change.

text: That all our knowledge begins with experience there can be no doubt.
zh: 毫无疑问，我们所有的知识都始于经验。
chunks: That all our knowledge begins
with experience there can be no doubt.

text: For, that bodies are heavy, and, consequently, that they fall when their supports are taken away, must have been known to him previously, by means of experience.
zh: 因为，身体很重，因此，当支撑物被拿走时，它们就会倒下，这是他之前通过经验所知道的。
chunks: For, that bodies are heavy, and, consequently,
that they fall
when their supports are taken away,
must have been known to him previously,
by means of experience.

text: If, moreover, it is not derived from any other proposition, unless from one equally involving the idea of necessity, it is absolutely priori.
zh: 此外，如果它不是从任何其他命题导出的，除非是从同样涉及必然性观念的命题导出的，那么它绝对是先验的。
chunks: If, moreover, it is not derived
from any other proposition,
unless from one equally involving the idea
of necessity,
it is absolutely priori.

text: Besides, without seeking for such examples of principles existing à priori in cognition, we might easily show that such principles are the indispensable basis of the possibility of experience itself, and consequently prove their existence à priori.
chunks: Besides, without seeking for such examples of principles existing à priori
in cognition, we might easily show
that such principles are the indispensable basis
of the possibility of experience itself,
and consequently prove their existence à priori.

text: Instead of thus trying to build without a foundation, it is rather to be expected that we should long ago have put the question, how the understanding can arrive at these à priori cognitions, and what is the extent, validity, and worth which they may possess?
chunks: Instead of thus trying to build without a foundation,
it is rather to be expected
that we should long ago have put the question,
how the understanding can arrive at these à priori cognitions,
and what is the extent, validity, and worth which they may possess?

text: The light dove cleaving in free flight the thin air, whose resistance it feels, might imagine that her movements would be far more free and rapid in airless space.
zh: 轻鸽在稀薄的空气中自由飞翔，它感受到空气的阻力，可能会想象她的动作在无空气的太空中会更加自由和迅速。
chunks: The light dove cleaving
in free flight the thin air,
whose resistance it feels, might imagine
that her movements would be far more free
and rapid in airless space.

text: In all judgements wherein the relation of a subject to the predicate is cogitated (I mention affirmative judgements only here; the application to negative will be very easy), this relation is possible in two different ways.
zh: 在主语与谓语关系经过深思熟虑的所有判断中（我只在这里提到肯定判断；应用于否定判断将非常容易），这种关系可以通过两种不同的方式实现。
chunks: In all judgements wherein the relation
of a subject
to the predicate is cogitated (I mention affirmative judgements only here;
the application to negative will be very easy),
this relation is possible in two different ways.

text: That “bodies are extended” is not an empirical judgement, but a proposition which stands firm à priori.
zh: “身体是延展的”并不是一个经验判断，而是一个先验的坚定命题。
chunks: That “bodies are extended” is not an empirical judgement,
but a proposition
which stands firm à priori.

text: that which happens,” and is consequently not contained in that conception.
zh: 发生的事情”，因此不包含在该概念中。
chunks: that which happens,
” and is consequently not contained
in that conception.

text: We might, indeed at first suppose that the proposition 7 + 5 = 12 is a merely analytical proposition, following (according to the principle of contradiction) from the conception of a sum of seven and five.
zh: 事实上，我们首先可以假设命题 7 + 5 = 12 只是一个分析命题，遵循（根据矛盾原理）七与五之和的概念。
chunks: We might, indeed at first suppose
that the proposition 7 + 5 = 12 is a merely analytical proposition,
following (according to the principle
of contradiction) from the conception
of a sum of seven and five.

text: The conception of the shortest is therefore fore wholly an addition, and by no analysis can it be extracted from our conception of a straight line.
zh: 因此，最短的概念完全是一个补充，任何分析都不能从我们的直线概念中提取出它。
chunks: The conception
of the shortest is therefore fore wholly an addition,
and by no analysis can it be extracted
from our conception
of a straight line.

text: In all communication of motion, action and reaction must always be equal.
zh: 在所有运动的交流中，作用和反作用力必须始终相等。
chunks: In all communication
of motion,
action and reaction must always be equal.

text: It is extremely advantageous to be able to bring a number of investigations under the formula of a single problem.
zh: 能够在一个问题的公式下进行多项研究是极其有利的。
chunks: It is extremely advantageous
to be able
to bring a number
of investigations under the formula
of a single problem.

text: For he would then have perceived that, according to his own argument, there likewise could not be any pure mathematical science, which assuredly cannot exist without synthetical propositions à priori—an absurdity from which his good understanding must have saved him.
chunks: For he would then have perceived that,
according to his own argument,
there likewise could not be any pure mathematical science,
which assuredly cannot exist without synthetical propositions à priori— an absurdity
from which his good understanding must have saved him.

text: This last question, which arises out of the above universal problem, would properly run thus: “How is metaphysics possible as a science?
zh: 从上述普遍问题中产生的最后一个问题可以这样表述：“形而上学作为一门科学如何可能？
chunks: This last question, which arises
out of the above universal problem,
would properly run thus:
“How is metaphysics possible
as a science?

text: An organon of pure reason would be a compendium of those principles according to which alone all pure cognitions à priori can be obtained.
zh: 纯粹理性的有机体将是那些原则的纲要，只有根据这些原则，才能获得所有纯粹的先验认知。
chunks: An organon
of pure reason would be a compendium
of those principles according
to which alone all pure cognitions à priori can be obtained.

text: And the object of our investigations, as it is not to be sought without, but, altogether within, ourselves, cannot remain concealed, and in all probability is limited enough to be completely surveyed and fairly estimated, according to its worth or worthlessness.
chunks: And the object of our investigations,
as it is not to be sought without, but,
altogether within, ourselves, cannot remain concealed, and in all probability is limited enough
to be completely surveyed and fairly estimated,
according to its worth or worthlessness.

text: Elements, and, secondly, a Doctrine of the Method of pure reason.
zh: 其次，纯粹理性方法学说。
chunks: Elements, and, secondly,
a Doctrine
of the Method
of pure reason.

text: The capacity for receiving representations (receptivity) through the mode in which we are affected by objects, objects, is called sensibility.
zh: 通过我们受物体影响的方式来接收表征（接受性）的能力称为感性。
chunks: The capacity for receiving representations (receptivity)
through the mode
in which we are affected
by objects, objects,
is called sensibility.

text: And accordingly we find existing in the mind à priori, the pure form of sensuous intuitions in general, in which all the manifold content of the phenomenal world is arranged and viewed under certain relations.
zh: 因此，我们发现存在于先验心灵中，即一般感性直觉的纯粹形式，其中现象世界的所有多种内容都在某些关系下被安排和观察。
chunks: And accordingly we find existing
in the mind à priori, the pure form
of sensuous intuitions in general, in which all the manifold content
of the phenomenal world is arranged
and viewed under certain relations.

text: In the science of transcendental æsthetic accordingly, we shall first isolate sensibility or the sensuous faculty, by separating from it all that is annexed to its perceptions by the conceptions of understanding, so that nothing be left but empirical intuition.
chunks: In the science of transcendental æsthetic accordingly,
we shall first isolate sensibility or the sensuous faculty,
by separating from it all that is annexed to its perceptions
by the conceptions of understanding,
so that nothing be left but empirical intuition.

text: Space is not a conception which has been derived from outward experiences.
zh: 空间不是一个源自外在经验的概念。
chunks: Space is not a conception
which has been derived from outward experiences.

text: Hence it follows that an à priori intuition (which is not empirical) lies at the root of all our conceptions of space.
zh: 因此，我们所有空间概念的根源都是先验直觉（非经验直觉）。
chunks: Hence it follows
that an à priori intuition
(which is not empirical) lies
at the root
of all our conceptions of space.

text: It must be originally intuition, for from a mere conception, no propositions can be deduced which go out beyond the conception, and yet this happens in geometry.
zh: 它必定是最初的直觉，因为仅仅从概念出发，无法推导出超出概念的命题，但在几何学中却发生了这种情况。
chunks: It must be originally intuition,
for from a mere conception,
no propositions can be deduced
which go out beyond the conception,
and yet this happens in geometry.

text: For neither absolute nor relative determinations of objects can be intuited prior to the existence of the things to which they belong, and therefore not à priori.
zh: 因为对象的绝对决定和相对决定都不能先于它们所属事物的存在而被直觉，因此也不是先验的。
chunks: For neither absolute nor relative determinations
of objects can be intuited prior
to the existence of the things
to which they belong,
and therefore not à priori.

text: For example, the proposition, “All objects are beside each other in space,” is valid only under the limitation that these things are taken as objects of our sensuous intuition.
chunks: For example, the proposition,
“All objects are beside each other
in space, ” is valid only
under the limitation that these things are taken
as objects of our sensuous intuition.

text: With regard to phenomena in general, we cannot think away time from them, and represent them to ourselves as out of and unconnected with time, but we can quite well represent to ourselves time void of phenomena.
zh: 对于一般的现象，我们不能将时间从它们中分离出来，并将它们呈现给我们自己，因为它们脱离了时间并且与时间无关，但是我们可以很好地向我们自己呈现没有现象的时间。
chunks: With regard to phenomena in general, we cannot think away time
from them, and represent them to ourselves as out
of and unconnected with time,
but we can quite well represent
to ourselves time void of phenomena.

text: Different times are merely parts of one and the same time.
zh: 不同的时间只是同一时间的一部分。
chunks: Different times are merely parts
of one and the same time.

text: § 6 Transcendental Exposition of the Conception of Time.
zh: § 6 时间概念的先验阐述。
chunks: § 6 Transcendental Exposition
of the Conception of Time.

text: For in that case, this form of the inward intuition can be represented prior to the objects, and consequently à priori.
zh: 因为在这种情况下，这种形式的内在直觉可以先于对象来表示，因此是先验的。
chunks: For in that case,
this form
of the inward intuition can be represented prior
to the objects,
and consequently à priori.

text: It is only of objective validity in regard to phenomena, because these are things which we regard as objects of our senses.
zh: 它仅对现象具有客观有效性，因为这些事物被我们视为我们感官的对象。
chunks: It is only of objective validity
in regard to phenomena,
because these are things
which we regard as objects
of our senses.

text: On the other hand, we deny to time all claim to absolute reality; that is, we deny that it, without having regard to the form of our sensuous intuition, absolutely inheres in things as a condition or property.
zh: 另一方面，我们否认时间对绝对现实的所有主张。也就是说，无论我们的感性直觉的形式如何，我们都否认它作为条件或属性绝对固有于事物中。
chunks: On the other hand, we deny
to time all claim to absolute reality;
that is, we deny that it, without having regard
to the form of our sensuous intuition,
absolutely inheres in things as a condition or property.

text: Time, therefore, is not to be regarded as an object, but as the mode of representation of myself as an object.
zh: 因此，时间不应被视为一个对象，而应被视为我作为对象的表征方式。
chunks: Time, therefore, is not
to be regarded as an object,
but as the mode
of representation of myself
as an object.

text: Time and space are, therefore, two sources of knowledge, from which, à priori, various synthetical cognitions can be drawn.
zh: 因此，时间和空间是知识的两个来源，可以先验地从中得出各种综合认知。
chunks: Time and space are, therefore,
two sources of knowledge,
from which,
à priori,
various synthetical cognitions can be drawn.

text: The latter has, indeed, this advantage, that the representations of space and time do not come in their way when they wish to judge of objects, not as phenomena, but merely in their relation to the understanding.
zh: 后者确实具有这样的优势，即当他们希望判断对象时，空间和时间的表征不会妨碍他们，而不是作为现象，而只是根据它们与理解的关系来判断。
chunks: The latter has, indeed, this advantage, that the representations of space
and time do not come
in their way when they wish
to judge of objects, not as phenomena, but merely
in their relation to the understanding.

text: In order to prevent any misunderstanding, it will be requisite, in the first place, to recapitulate, as clearly as possible, what our opinion is with respect to the fundamental nature of our sensuous cognition in general.
zh: 为了防止任何误解，首先有必要尽可能清楚地概括我们对一般感性认知的基本性质的看法。
chunks: In order to prevent any misunderstanding,
it will be requisite, in the first place,
to recapitulate, as clearly as possible,
what our opinion is with respect to the fundamental nature
of our sensuous cognition in general.

text: The difference between a confused and a clear representation is merely logical and has nothing to do with content.
zh: 混乱的表示和清晰的表示之间的区别仅仅是逻辑上的，与内容无关。
chunks: The difference
between a confused
and a clear representation is merely logical
and has nothing
to do with content.

text: In the first place, it is evident that both present us, with very many apodeictic and synthetic propositions à priori, but especially space—and for this reason we shall prefer it for investigation at present.
zh: 首先，很明显，两者都向我们展示了许多先验的绝经和综合命题，但尤其是空间——因此，我们目前更倾向于用它来进行研究。
chunks: In the first place, it is evident
that both present us, with very many apodeictic
and synthetic propositions à priori, but especially space—
and for this reason we shall prefer it
for investigation at present.

text: Is it a pure à priori, or is it an empirical intuition?
zh: 它是纯粹的先验，还是经验的直觉？
chunks: Is it a pure à priori,
or is it an empirical intuition?

text: But this difficulty is common to every theory.
zh: 但这个困难对于每个理论来说都是共同的。
chunks: But this difficulty is common
to every theory.

text: But (illusory) appearance never can be attributed as a predicate to an object, for this very reason, that it attributes to this object in itself that which belongs to it only in relation to our sensuous faculty, or to the subject in general, e.g., the two handles which were formerly ascribed to Saturn.
chunks: But (illusory) appearance never can be attributed as a predicate to an object,
for this very reason, that it attributes
